decisions.reason: Both the shipped record (listing the OnlineFirst year 2013, short title, and DOI 10.1177/0956797613508412) and blind target 0 (listing the 2014 print reference) identify the same target original article by Wilkins and Kaiser (2014) in Psychological Science (25, 439-446), whose three studies are directly re-tested by Studies 1, 2, 3a, and 3b.

decisions.quote:
In three studies, Wilkins and Kaiser found that both chronic and experimental salience of racial progress in the United States
increased the perceptions of anti-White bias only among people high in status-legitimizing beliefs (SLBs). We conducted four
preregistered high-powered replications of this research. Studies 1, 2, and 3a were close replications of studies 1–3, respectively.
Study 3b was a close replication that included an additional experimental condition.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind classify the record as 'replication'. The authors collected new data across four fresh MTurk participant samples (Studies 1, 2, 3a, and 3b) to re-test the published findings of Wilkins and Kaiser (2014).
